hints: Expand the numerator $(\sin\theta+\cos\theta)^2$ into three separate terms.
Use the Pythagorean identity $\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta \equiv 1$ to simplify the numerator.
Divide the remaining term $2\sin\theta\cos\theta$ by $\cos^2\theta$ and apply $\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta} \equiv \tan\theta$.
walkthrough:
Expand the squared binomial in the numerator:
$$(\sin\theta+\cos\theta)^2 = \sin^2\theta + 2\sin\theta\cos\theta + \cos^2\theta$$

Apply the Pythagorean identity $\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta \equiv 1$ to simplify the numerator:
$$\text{Numerator} = (\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta) + 2\sin\theta\cos\theta - 1 = 1 + 2\sin\theta\cos\theta - 1 = 2\sin\theta\cos\theta$$

Substitute the simplified numerator back into the algebraic fraction:
$$\frac{(\sin\theta+\cos\theta)^2-1}{\cos^2\theta} = \frac{2\sin\theta\cos\theta}{\cos^2\theta} = \frac{2\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}$$

Apply the quotient identity $\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta} \equiv \tan\theta$ to conclude the proof:
$$\frac{2\sin\theta}{\cos\theta} = 2\tan\theta$$

ai_rubric.Trigonometric Identities: Expands the bracket $(\sin\theta+\cos\theta)^2$ to three terms and applies $\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta\equiv 1$ to simplify the numerator to $2\sin\theta\cos\theta$ (M1). Uses $\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}\equiv\tan\theta$ (M1). Concludes convincingly with $2\tan\theta$ with no errors (A1).

hints: Replace the left-hand side with $2\tan\theta$ using the identity proved in part (a).
Rearrange into $5\tan^3\theta - 2\tan\theta = 0$ and factor out $\tan\theta$ rather than dividing by it.
Solve $\tan\theta = 0$ and $\tan^2\theta = \frac{2}{5}$ for all values of $\theta$ in the interval $-90^\circ < \theta < 90^\circ$.
walkthrough:
Substitute the identity from part (a) into the equation and rearrange all terms to one side:
$$2\tan\theta = 5\tan^3\theta \implies 5\tan^3\theta - 2\tan\theta = 0$$

Factorise the equation into linear and quadratic trigonometric factors:
$$\tan\theta(5\tan^2\theta - 2) = 0 \implies \tan\theta = 0 \quad \text{or} \quad \tan^2\theta = \frac{2}{5}$$

State all three solutions in ascending order:
$$\theta = -32.3^\circ, \quad 0^\circ, \quad 32.3^\circ$$

ai_rubric.Solving Trigonometric Equations: Sets $5\tan^3\theta = 2\tan\theta$ and factorises to obtain $\tan\theta = 0$ or $\tan^2\theta = \frac{2}{5}$ (M1). Obtains at least two correct angles (A1). Obtains all three correct solutions $\theta = -32.3^\circ, 0^\circ, 32.3^\circ$ with no extras in the range (A1).
